newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent edges higher on US stock data, weather.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent edges higher on US stock data, weather.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil was moderately higher at midday on Friday, but volumes were light in a thin Christmas market.
February Brent was trading up 19 cents at $23.58 a barrel at 1250 GMT, having broken through the $23.55 level that capped the contract in both Monday and Tuesday's session.
"It might push above there if NYMEX takes off," said one trader who pegged the next resistance level at $23.74 in line with where a downside trendline cuts the daily chart.
Gas oil was $2.50 higher at $218.00 a tonne.

Traders said both complexes had been helped by bullish oil stock data which showed an unexpectedly sharp draw in U.S. crude stocks as well as a small decline in distillates as opposed to an expected build.

The U.S. EIA data released on Thursday showed a 6.1 million draw in U.S. crude stocks to 290.6 million barrels, while the American Petroleum Institute estimated a 5.16 million barrel draw to 297.87 million barrels.
The EIA said distillate stocks fell 1.5 million barrels and the API estimated a 1.89 million draw in distillates.
Traders said gas oil had also been helped higher by arctic weather conditions which have hit most of Europe.
